assigned.title: Profiles become usable: a picker, a switch, and a create
assigned.acceptance: A person can see who they are watching as, switch, and create a profile. THE BACKEND IS COMPLETE AND REVIEWED AND NOTHING RENDERS IT: /api/v1/profiles and /api/v1/profiles/selection exist with handlers, contracts and tests, and there is no picker, no switch, no create and no avatar anywhere in the application. REQUIRED: the active profile is visible in the shell at all times, because every progress and watchlist row in this product is profile-scoped and a viewer who cannot see which profile is active cannot understand their own continue-watching list. REQUIRED: profile selection goes through the existing selection route and the existing ProfileScope, never through a client-held id -- PL-0405 recorded a forgeable-scope defect and this UI must not reintroduce it, which is why a security review is required. REQUIRED: switching profiles invalidates any cached profile-scoped view rather than leaving another profile's rows on screen.
assigned.notes: PROPOSED FOR gpt-architect RULING, round 80. Created unowned as part of the WINDOWS PRODUCT COMPLETION phase board so the proposal is machine-readable rather than prose, and NOT claimed before the verdict.

typecheck.evidence: EXECUTED on ead34dc. npm run typecheck at the root, own invocation, turbo 21/21, exit 0. Also npm run lint 11/11 with zero problems and zero warnings, and npx turbo run build --force 11/11 with apps/web compiled successfully -- the build is not a required gate here but a new route that does not build is not a route, and /profiles appears in the emitted route manifest as a dynamic (server-rendered on demand) entry, which is what export const dynamic = force-dynamic asks for. THREE LINT FINDINGS WERE FIXED RATHER THAN SUPPRESSED, and one of them was a real defect: react-hooks/set-state-in-effect flagged the picker's initial load, and the fix was not a disable comment but rewriting the effect as an async closure with a live flag -- the component previously had no unmount guard at all, so a viewer who navigated away before the list resolved would have had setState called on an unmounted component. The other two were an unescaped apostrophe in the heading and an unused catch binding, the latter now an intentional bare catch whose comment states that the parse error is discarded because it quotes the offending bytes.

unit.evidence: EXECUTED on ead34dc. cd apps/web && npx vitest run over the three new suites -> avatar 15, profiles-client 20, profile-ui 14, exit 0; monorepo npx turbo run test --force -> 20/20 packages, exit 0, with apps/web at 63 files / 1075 tests, up from 1026 last round, and every other package unchanged. WHAT THE 49 TESTS ARE FOR, BY THE PROPERTY THEY DEFEND. NO CLIENT-HELD SCOPE, WHICH IS THE SECURITY CORE: listProfiles is asserted to send no body, no query and no id, and the URL is asserted not to contain a question mark -- PL-0405 recorded a forgeable-scope defect and a ?profileId= on a read is exactly how it comes back. selectProfile is asserted to be the only function that sends an id, to send it in the body of the selection route and never in the path or a query, and to pass a malformed id straight through rather than pre-judging it, because isMintedProfileId is the single authority and a second pattern here would answer request_malformed where the first answers profile_unavailable -- itself a small oracle. A source scan over all three modules asserts none of them reads localStorage, sessionStorage, document.cookie, useSearchParams, URLSearchParams or window.location, so there is no client-side source of a profile id anywhere in the directory. NOTHING UNEXPECTED REACHES THE DOM: four tests cover the unreadable path, including that an HTML error page, a script tag and a token-bearing JSON body all produce a detail containing none of their bytes -- only the zod issue PATHS and the HTTP status. A REFUSAL IS AN ANSWER, NOT A FAILURE: a 403 refused body and a 503 unavailable body both classify as answered with their reason trail intact, because collapsing them would throw away the only thing the viewer or support can act on. THE ORDER IS THE SERVER'S: three profiles served in a deliberately non-alphabetical, non-chronological order come back in exactly that order, and a source rule forbids .sort, .reverse, .toSorted and .toReversed in the picker, because oldest-first is stated in profilesResponseSchema as a promise about muscle memory. THE SWITCH CLAUSE IS ASSERTED STRUCTURALLY: the selected branch must contain await reload() and router.refresh() and must not contain activeProfileId:, so the picker cannot start agreeing with itself while the page shows another profile's rows. THE BADGE IS UNCONDITIONAL: AppShell is rendered with react-dom/server on three different pathnames, with and without a status badge, and profile-badge is present in all three -- no page passes a profile prop, so no route can opt out by forgetting one. FIRST PAINT MAKES NO CLAIM: the badge's first paint is asserted to contain no Choose profile, no Watching as and no href, and the picker's to be aria-busy with Loading profiles and no profile-tile and no no profiles yet -- an empty-household message shown while still asking is the worst thing a picker can say. AVATAR STABILITY IS A PROPERTY, NOT AN EXAMPLE: 500 seeds are asserted to stay in [0,360) and to spread across more than 200 distinct hues, renaming a profile is asserted not to change its hue, and the module is source-scanned for Date., Math.random, process.env, fetch(, globalThis and crypto. with a non-vacuity check. Initials are tested against an astral character and a combining sequence, which displayName[0] would split.

e2e.evidence: EXECUTED Playwright runs at ead34dc, both modes, plus an independent live-server witness. Production, the default: cd e2e && npx playwright test --project=api --project=chromium -> 73 tests, 61 passed, 12 skipped, 0 failed. Development: LIBERTY_E2E_WEB_MODE=development, same projects -> 73 tests, 70 passed, 3 skipped, 0 failed. Both counts are IDENTICAL to the round-82 run, which is the point: this task adds a route and a topbar element to a shell every existing spec renders, and the regression evidence is that nothing moved. WHAT THIS GATE DOES NOT COVER, STATED PLAINLY. There is no e2e spec for the profile journey itself, because e2e/** is outside this task's allowedPaths and widening the surface a second time to write one would have been reservation inflation for a file the E2E lane owns. So the executed suite is REGRESSION evidence, not feature evidence, and the feature is evidenced below by a different instrument instead. I recommend a narrow follow-up owning a profiles journey spec; I have not filed it, because PW-0601's certification matrix may already own the row and filing a duplicate is worse than naming the gap here. THE INDEPENDENT WITNESS, which is not a spec reading itself. A real next dev server on 127.0.0.1:3999 was driven with curl against the real handlers and the real in-memory adapter: GET /api/v1/profiles returned outcome listed with 0 profiles and activeProfileId null; POST /api/v1/profiles with the exact three-field strict body returned created with a minted uuid; POST /api/v1/profiles/selection with that id returned selected and the reason selectable_profile_of_account; the next GET returned 1 profile with activeProfileId equal to the minted id. A selection of a well-formed uuid this session does not own returned HTTP 403 with outcome refused and profile_unavailable -- the non-oracle answer -- so the forgeable-scope property holds against the live route and not only in the transport tests. GET /profiles returned 200 and the served bytes contained the escaped heading, Loading profiles and profile-badge-checking, which is the first paint the unit suite asserts, reaching a browser. GET / and GET /search both served profile-badge, so the at all times clause is witnessed on routes this task did not touch. THE DEPLOYMENT BRANCH WAS WITNESSED TOO, on next start against the production build on 127.0.0.1:3998: /profiles served 200 while GET /api/v1/profiles answered HTTP 503 with outcome unavailable and storage_not_configured. That is the honest degraded state the picker is built to render rather than showing an empty household, and it is storage_not_configured rather than authentication_not_configured only because storage is checked first -- the authentication residual PW-0403 owns is behind it, not absent. ONE NARROWING, the same one PL-0704 recorded and it has not changed: the browser under test is NOT the pinned revision. The container ships Chromium 1194 and @playwright/test 1.62.1 requires 1234, so a symlink registry presenting 1194 under the 1234 names was built in a scratch directory and selected with PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH; nothing in the repository changed for it. The first attempt this round failed with Executable does not exist because the 1194 tree lays its binary out as chrome-linux/headless_shell while 1.62.1 expects chrome-headless-shell-linux64/chrome-headless-shell -- the registry now maps that layout explicitly, which is worth recording because the previous round's registry would silently stop working after any browser bump. Only api and chromium ran, so this says nothing about WebKit, Firefox or mobile-safari, and no claim is made that the CI job will be green.

recommended.title: Artwork, end to end, because a media application without images is a list
recommended.acceptance: Titles have artwork, and getting it does not become a new way to fetch arbitrary URLs. MEASURED STARTING POINT: there are zero images in this product at any layer -- no next/image, no img tag, and no poster, artwork, backdrop or thumbnail key anywhere in packages/contracts/src. Posters are CSS gradients. REQUIRED: artwork is a contract change first, reviewed, with dimensions and a rights basis beside the URL rather than a bare string, because an image is content and CONTENT_RIGHTS.md does not exempt it. REQUIRED: the host allowlist and transport rules the rest of this repository already enforces apply to image origins too; SECURITY.md's 'never proxy arbitrary client-provided URLs' is not weakened for pictures, which is why this task carries a security review. REQUIRED: an absent image is a designed state, not a broken one -- the existing gradient placeholder stays as the fallback rather than a broken-image icon. REQUIRED: next/image remote patterns are pinned to the allowlist, not opened to a wildcard.

recommended.title: Offline, degraded and error states a desktop application needs
recommended.acceptance: The application behaves honestly when the network, the backend or the sidecar is unavailable. There is no offline handling of any kind today -- no navigator.onLine, no service worker, no offline banner, no retry-on-reconnect. THIS MATTERS MORE ON THE DESKTOP THAN IT DID ON THE WEB: docs/DESKTOP_PLAYBACK.md section 8 accepts that an offline desktop cannot resolve playback at all, and requires that failure be surfaced as an honest unavailable outcome rather than an empty candidate list -- so the UI half of that ruling is this task. REQUIRED: a network-state signal and a visible degraded mode that names what is unavailable. REQUIRED: recovery on reconnect without a manual reload. REQUIRED: the sidecar being down is a DISTINCT state from the backend being down and from the network being down, because the three have different remedies and collapsing them produces a support burden. REQUIRED: no state invents content; an offline home shows what it has and says so.
